successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Roman Dacia's land without Banat: Decebalus 'lost some territories in the vicinity of the Danube' in 102, drawn as Banat, the place the Decebalus page names for the 'newly occupied Roman territory'…

ledger.x: 85: the Dacian kingdom under King Duras raids Moesia.
88: the Romans defeat the Dacians near Tapae.
89: after Domitian's peace Decebalus is a client king of Rome.
101: Trajan's first war ends the client relation.
102: Decebalus stays on the throne as a client king.
105: the client relation ends with the second war.
106: the Dacian kingdom ends and Dacia becomes a Roman province.

wars.name: Domitian's Dacian War
wars.outcome: Two wars: Dacian raids on Moesia in 85 and 86, Cornelius Fuscus defeated at Tapae, Tettius Julianus's victory near Tapae in 88; Rome made peace after Domitian's defeat by the Marcomanni, Decebalus became a client king and received eight million sesterces…

wars.name: Trajan's first Dacian War
wars.outcome: Decebalus was defeated in 102 and surrendered territory, equipment and agreed to Roman garrisons and not crossing the Danube; a Roman garrison and acting governor were set at Sarmizegetusa.

wars.name: Trajan's second Dacian War
wars.outcome: Sarmizegetusa fell and Decebalus killed himself in 106; the southern half of Dacia was annexed as the province Dacia Traiana, the northern half remained free.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the Danube is the limit towards Moesia.
